## What this settles

1. **The extracted node is not stuck.** Its discharge at ss/-40 C is monotonically falling across all 8 samples: confirmed, 327.8 mV at +0.5 ms down to 176.4 mV at +17 ms. It is the same monotonic discharge as the schematic export, on a longer time constant -- not a held stale valid.
2. **The time constant, not the endpoint, is what moved.** At the parent testbench's own sample instant the two netlists read 33.63 mV (schematic) and 303.4 mV (extracted), a factor of 9.02; the extracted node needs roughly the whole 17 ms window to reach the level the schematic export reaches in 2 ms.
3. **The core's own discharge is not what moved.** Over the same window V(VREF) on the same DUT differs between the two netlists by at most 26 mV anywhere on the grid sampled here (3.9 mV at ss/-40 C, the failing family), against a `BIAS_OK` difference that reaches 270 mV at the same instant and the same corner. The reference core gives up its charge at essentially the same rate on both netlists; what changed by an order of magnitude is the `BIAS_OK`/`NOKX` output net's own parasitic RC. (At tt/+27 C both `BIAS_OK` readings are sub-millivolt on both netlists -- that corner is a reference point showing the check has nothing to measure where it passes, not a second data point about the mechanism.)
